title: Host Lifecycle Concierge: staged cordon, prioritized eviction, and capacity escrow API
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a Host Lifecycle Concierge service and developer-facing API that coordinates node cordon/drain, issues time-bounded capacity escrow tokens, and orchestrates KV-cache prewarm lanes to preserve throughput and SLOs during maintenance. This feature targets Dedicated fleets and Private deployments and is intended to reduce tail latency and capacity shocks during upgrades or planned decommissions.
background: Operators currently rely on ad-hoc scripts and manual maintenance windows. Large drains cause throughput cliffs because cold KV caches and abrupt eviction of high-priority traffic create SLO regressions. Prior attempts at simple staged drains reduced incidents but required per-app configuration and manual reservations. We need a single coordinator that encodes policy, exposes a small API, and integrates with autoscaler and routing layers.
goals: Provide an API to request/issue capacity escrow tokens that reserve a fraction of throughput for a node during a maintenance window
Implement staged cordon and prioritized eviction workflow that demotes low-priority traffic first
Orchestrate KV-cache prewarm lanes (preheat tasks) so model KV caches are warmed before traffic transitions
Expose telemetry and SLO impact estimates in Console for each scheduled maintenance
Enable safe rollback and forced-abort paths with automatic rebalancing
out_of_scope: New autoscaler heuristics (only integration points provided)
Application-level graceful shutdown hooks (we will provide hooks but not rewrite apps)
acceptance_criteria: API: /escrow/request returns time-bounded escrow token and expected reserved RPS; tokens enforceable by routing layer
Workflow: scheduled cordon->prewarm->evict(low-priority)->evict(medium)->final-drain completes without >2% 99th latency uplift on synthetic workload
KV prewarm: preheat jobs achieve >90% KV hit-rate on warmed keys within configured prewarm window
Canary: rollout on 2 dedicated pools with one-repeatable simulated maintenance run without customer-facing errors
Observability: Console shows per-host escrow, estimated SLO delta, and a link to the active maintenance run
design_review_notes: 2025-01-22: PM and SRE requested explicit escrow token lifetime and a soft-fallback policy to avoid over-reserving capacity
2025-01-28: Security requested audit events for escrow issuance and token usage (added event hooks)
Design decision: escrow tokens will be JSON Web Tokens signed by control-plane KMS and include reserved RPS and expiry
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Control-plane API and token issuance, minimal enforcement hooks in proxy (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Staged cordon runner and eviction priority engine; integrate with autoscaler (3 weeks)
Phase 3: KV prewarm orchestration and preheat worker set (3 weeks)
Phase 4: Console integration, telemetry, and canary rollout (2 weeks)
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Spike complete. Validated token-issuance model using signed JWTs; prototype proxy honors token header for routing reservation
2025-01-21: Implemented initial escrow API and a fake-enforcement mode for local testing. Early feedback: token format good but needs prewarm hint field

2025-01-30: Built cordon runner skeleton. Decided to use eviction priority buckets (low/medium/high) driven by route labels. PM advised adding per-route weight overrides for customers with strict SLAs

2025-02-05: Prewarm worker skeleton implemented; first end-to-end run in staging warmed KV for small models. Observed cold-start spike on larger models; will add multi-stage prewarm (small->large keysets)
2025-02-09: Integration tests added for token expiry and forced-abort. Preparing canary checklist and monitoring playbook
risks: Over-reservation of capacity causing wasted resources if escrow model is too conservative
Coordination lags between prewarm completion and routing change can still produce short SLO blips
Complexity for customers with mixed criticality traffic; risk of policy misconfiguration
Security: improperly scoped tokens could be replayed by misbehaving proxies (we mitigate with nonce and short TTL)
mitigations: Start with conservative default escrow (2-5% per concurrent drain) and iterate with telemetry
Add explicit prewarm-complete signal that gate switches in routing layer
Provide per-team sane defaults and a guided console UX for weight overrides
Use signed tokens, nonce validation, and short-lived TTL; audit events for every issuance and use
qa_plan: Synthetic traffic sims comparing baseline vs concierge-run with mixed priority routes
Chaos test: random forced-abort mid-prewarm to ensure rollback keeps latency within SLO
Load test: drain 20% of hosts concurrently with escrow tokens enforced to validate autoscaler interactions
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal canary on staging fleets (manual)
Stage 1: pilot with 2 low-risk customers on Dedicated (opt-in) for 2 weeks
Stage 2: broader gradual enablement with telemetry-based gating
Stage 3: GA with console defaults and docs
notes: We intentionally separate the issuance/enforcement boundary so enforcement can be toggled for gradual rollout. Follow-ups: add RBAC for who can request large escrows, and expose simulated SLO delta in the Console scheduling flow. PM requested an optional 'business window' label to align maintenance with customer timezones.
